- **Starting from a fresh high instead:** 11 / 33 / 32 / 27 / 43%. That supports §6's "~30-45%" for the long samples.
- **Back above 107.11 within 60 sessions:** 72 to 79% with an edge, 55% with none.
- **Equity at or below 50 within 250 sessions, constant 0.86:** 0.1 / 2.3 / 3.3 / 1.5 / 15.7%.
- **Same, with the §6 PAUSE cut to 1 NVDL share modelled:** 0.08 / 1.8 / 2.5 / 1.0 / 14.1%.

Results move by only a few points with 1-night or 20-night blocks.

**Live record against the plan:**
- **Return:** over 27 nights, -0.24% per unit invested (sd 2.32), t -0.54 against zero; 90% CI -1.00 to +0.52.
- **Against the planned +0.30:** z -1.21 using the live sd, or -1.05 using the model sd (one-sided p about 0.12).
- **Against +0.25 and +0.35:** z -1.10 and -1.32.
- **On total equity:** -0.154%/night against 0.30 × 0.847 = 0.254, z -1.10.

That is about one standard error below plan, and not significant either way. Showing a +0.30 edge at t 2 needs about 315 nights.

What actually happened:
- **NVDL over the same 27 nights:** just +0.15%/night (t 0.27).
- **The live baskets** (mostly not NVDA-only) lagged NVDL by 0.39%/night (t -1.23).
- **On the 3 NVDA-only nights** live tracked the model within 0.4 points.
- **NVDL's last 4 nights** compounded to -10.5%, the 3rd percentile of all 4-night stretches.
- **This week NVDA lost 5.1% across the four overnight holds while gaining 0.85% intraday.** That is the opposite of the pattern the strategy relies on. One week is noise.
issues: The task assumes NVDA-2x-only nights start 2026-10-12, but the 10/12 night held METU x2 + NVDL. Only 3 of the 27 live nights (10/13, 10/14, 10/15) were NVDA-2x only. The other 24 held NVDL+AMZU, NVDL+METU(+NVDX) or METU+AAPU, so comparing the 27-night record to an NVDA-2x backtest is not like for like. Those baskets were also less volatile: live sd 2.32 per unit invested vs NVDL 2.66.

Sample size dominates. The standard error of a 27-night mean is about 0.45-0.51%/night, larger than the +0.30 planning edge itself. z of -1.05 to -1.32 against plan and t of -0.54 against zero are both inconclusive. About 315 nights are needed for t = 2 on a +0.30 edge. The 9% drawdown is only 1.1-1.4x likelier with no edge than with one, so it should not be read as evidence that the edge has decayed.

Regime and hindsight: NVDL's sample (Dec 2022 to Oct 2026) sits inside NVDA's large bull run, and NVDA was picked after the fact. On the 2x-NVDA proxy the yearly mean ranged from -0.46%/night in 2022 (a 75% loss for the year) to +0.71 in 2024, with 2023 at +0.05 and 2025 at +0.12. Trailing 120/250 t-stats are only 1.3-1.8. Bootstraps that resample the historical mean inherit this drift; the runs reset to +0.30 and to zero bracket it. Results depend heavily on the sample: P(-20% within 60 sessions) is 21% on last year's data vs 40% on the long samples, and P(equity <= 50) is 0.1% vs 2-3%.

The 2x proxy is 2 × NVDA close-to-open minus a fixed 4bp/night. Measured gap between NVDL and the proxy, earnings excluded: -1.6 to -4.7bp/night in 2024-26, with only 0.16-0.22% sd per night. Volatility decay from daily compounding does not apply to a hold that starts at the close reset and ends at the next open, so the proxy leaves out only fees and financing, the gap between the ETF's opening print and 2x NVDA's open, our 15:52/09:31 execution versus close and open, and ETF/issuer risk. NVDL's 2023 opening prints are noisy: its overnight beta to NVDA was 1.51 in 2023 vs about 2.0 from 2024.

Earnings exclusion: NVDA report dates for 2015-2026 come from the public record (from memory, not a full feed). 2023-05-24 was confirmed with get_earnings_calendar, and 2025-11 through 2026-08 match the repo research docs. A volume-spike cross-check flagged 8 dates where a different day had higher volume nearby; I believe all 8 are correct report dates, not errors. Excluded: 47 earnings nights from the proxy, 15 from NVDL. The 2019-01-25 and 2022-08-05 pre-market pre-announcements are kept in, flagged only.

Distributions were not added back from a dividend feed; Robinhood daily bars are split-adjusted only. As a stand-in, the 'clean' NVDL series replaces 58 nights where NVDL and 2x NVDA differ by more than 1% with the proxy. Almost all are Dec 2022 to Jan 2024, including 2023-12-26 at -10.2%, likely a distribution. The trailing windows contain only one such night (2026-05-01). §3(f) is +0.331 raw vs +0.318 clean, so the sign is unaffected. The NVDL 10/28 ex-date still needs checking per §8.
The 10/16 opens (NVDL 32.745, NVDA 216.53) come from the first 1-minute bar, because the daily bar was not yet published at 09:38 ET. The last night in the sample is 10/15 to 10/16.

Bootstrap assumptions: constant 0.86 invested; the 250-session horizon ignores the roughly 4 earnings nights the rules would hold in cash; the §3(f) switch is not modelled (it would lower the equity <= 50 odds in slow bear markets and cost in V-shaped rebounds). The PAUSE variant approximates 1 NVDL share as $33. Monte Carlo standard error is at most 0.35 points. Results are stable within about ±5 points across 1/5/20-night blocks; the proxy's equity <= 50 odds range 3.3-5.3%.

Ledger inconsistency in state.json: the night_returns 'pct' field changes basis partway through. Up to about 9/29 it is P&L over equity; from 9/30 it is P&L over the amount invested. Example: 10/14 shows -5.61, which is -4.90/87.39 invested, but -4.73% of equity. Live statistics here were recomputed from trades.csv fills and equity.csv EOD; total P&L matches (-4.65 vs state -4.67).

The high of 107.11 is taken from state.json and does not appear in equity.csv, whose highest EOD is 107.02 on 10/12. The -9.02% drawdown equals exactly the 4 overnight losses (-9.66 total). The rolling 20-session §6 trigger drifts away from the all-time-high version once 10/12 leaves the window, roughly 16 sessions from now.

Not established: whether the live lag behind the NVDL model (-0.39%/night, t -1.23) comes from basket choice or execution. On the 3 NVDA-only nights live tracked the model within about 0.4 points, which points to the earlier non-NVDA baskets. This week NVDA fell 5.1% across the overnight holds while rising 0.85% intraday, the reverse of the strategy's premise. The worst night, 10/14 into 10/15, came ahead of TSM's earnings; RULES_v3 §6 defers any decision on such nights to the 2027-01-11 review.
